`builder.py` works on a checkout with tools, and the words follow. `Plane` becomes `Tools`, and every `world` in names, parameters, keys, docstrings, comments, messages and the usage line becomes `checkout`: the usage line reads `builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`, the numbers key `world` becomes `checkout`, `world_head` becomes `head` in the numbers and the function that computes it becomes `head()`. In the role text `a world` becomes `a checkout` and nothing else in it changes. The checkout must be a git checkout: a directory without `.git` is a usage error, exit 2, before any run directory exists, so the branches that record `not a git checkout` and a null head go, and `head` is always a commit. `plans` leaves `HIDDEN`. `test_builder.py` already uses the new names; the tests whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour and the rest of the suite must stay green.

The documents follow after the build, by the attended agent: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the seed template and the seeds say checkout and tools; the notes of v0.1 to v0.4 keep their words as history, and one sentence in `AGENTS.md` maps the old words to the new.

From the review of the first build: the module docstring lists `diff.patch (what the run left in the checkout; absent when it left nothing)` and `record_diff`'s docstring says the patch is absent when the run left nothing, since that is what the build made true and the tests pin; the comment above `HIDDEN` no longer speaks of planning; a directory whose `.git` is not git's, a stray file, is refused as `not a git checkout`, and a checkout with no commit as `the checkout has no commit`; the joined patch is bound once; the two docstrings that said `the five functions of the tools` and `Not a function of the tools` say `the five tools` and `not one of the tools`.

From the review of the second build: a checkout is the root of its own repository, which `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run in it must name, and git runs with `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` removed from its environment, so a subdirectory of a repository, with or without a `.git` of its own, and a directory the environment points elsewhere are refused as `not a git checkout`, while a worktree, whose `.git` is a file, is a checkout; a git that cannot run before the run is a usage error naming git, never a traceback; the comment above the guard explains both its halves; the module docstring says `reachable only through five tools` and no longer names a version.

From the review of the third build: the two diffs of `record_diff` run with `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, so neither the environment, nor the configuration, nor a `.gitattributes` in the checkout can replace the patch with a program's output; a git that ran and failed before the run directory exists, whichever call it was, is a usage error carrying git's own message, exit 2, and a good checkout is not called `not a git checkout` for a failure of git's.

2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a checkout until its tests pass.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"
5	
6	The checkout is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five tools:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the checkout and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the checkout's tests in a container with no network and the
9	checkout mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the checkout, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl
13	(every HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per

100	    """The builder's report: what it changed in the checkout, and whether the tests pass."""

105	    )

107	    failing: list[str] = Field(description="Test names if red.")

112	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip

115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
119	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
120	        items = getattr(report, field)
121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]

129	    """The tools: what the model can do to the checkout, and the record of it."""

131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox

145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the checkout: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the checkout: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the checkout
161	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
162	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere

170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:

174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the checkout: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is

178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the checkout root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
187	            if rel == ".":

197	            return f"error: {e}"

201	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
202	        """Read a file of the checkout as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
204	
205	        Args:
206	            path: The file to read, relative to the checkout root.
207	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
208	        """

210	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
211	            if not p.is_file():
212	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
213	            start = max(1, int(start))
214	            out: list[str] = []
215	            n = nbytes = 0
216	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
217	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
218	                    if i < start:
219	                        continue
220	                    size = len(line.encode())
221	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
222	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
223	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
224	                            break
225	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
226	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
227	                    else:
228	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
229	                    n += 1
230	                    nbytes += size

232	            return f"error: {e}"

240	
241	        Args:
242	            path: The file to write, relative to the checkout root.
243	            content: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

317	class Sandbox:
318	    """Where the checkout's tests run: a container, no network, the checkout mounted read-only.
319	
320	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the checkout's own locked dependencies,
321	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
322	    """
323	
324	    @staticmethod
325	    def image(checkout: Path) -> str:
326	        """The image name for this checkout: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
327	        h = hashlib.sha256((checkout / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (checkout / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
328	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
329	
330	    @staticmethod
331	    def ensure_image(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
332	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
333	        name = Sandbox.image(checkout)
334	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
335	        if seen.returncode == 0:
336	            return name
337	        built = subprocess.run(
338	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
339	            # factory never runs from inside the checkout.
340	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(checkout / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(checkout)],
341	            capture_output=True,
342	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
343	        )
344	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
345	        if built.returncode != 0:
346	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")
